A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable. v1 Appendices A-D match v4 Appendices D-G; v4 adds three preceding appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier-transfer experiments, texture and frequency analyses, distribution measurements and synthetic-data scaling results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds VAE reconstruction, object detection, semantic segmentation and synthetic-test results in Tables 1-4.

M1.justification: The generation procedure, prompting schemes and original diagnostic framework remain unchanged. SAM3 annotation and additional downstream architectures support new evaluations rather than modifying the studied generation method.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds object detection and semantic segmentation, substantially extending the classification-only task coverage in v1. These tasks reuse the retained ImageNet subset and synthetic images, with SAM3-generated boxes and masks; no new source image domain is introduced.

E2.justification: The existing generator comparisons and real-data references are retained. Detection and segmentation use previously evaluated SD1.5, SD3.0, Flux-dev, Lumina2 and Qwen-Image. Faster-RCNN and DeepLabv3 are downstream evaluators, not new competing generators.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce VAE-reconstruction controls, SAM3 annotation of both real and synthetic images, Faster-RCNN and DeepLabv3 training, and detection/segmentation metrics. Detection uses 26 epochs and batch size 16; segmentation uses 30 epochs and batch size 20. The retained classification experiment keeps its reported sample counts and training budget.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a reconstruction control isolating VAE-related degradation. Appendix C adds analysis of synthetic-domain performance to investigate poor fit versus poor transfer. These are substantive new diagnostic analyses; the original texture, frequency, diversity, scaling and visual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 add substantial results while retaining the original plotted findings. Detection AP is 11.9 for SD1.5 versus 3.1 for Qwen; segmentation mIoU is 49.3 versus 12.6. Qwen classification accuracy is 97.9 on synthetic tests versus 9.9 on real tests. New summaries contain inconsistencies: Table 4 gives real-data mIoU 47.6 versus 75.2 in Table 3, and SDXL accuracy 30.5 versus approximately 33% in the retained Figure 1.

T1.justification: The spectral power-law relation, frequency conditions and density/coverage explanations are retained. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim that distribution narrowing undermines label-image alignment with a claim about real-data distribution coverage. The central contributions concerning declining training utility, texture/frequency deficiencies and diversity loss remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly attributes substantial high-frequency degradation to VAE reconstruction. Appendix C interprets strong synthetic-test performance as excluding poor fit and supporting an easier, more separable synthetic manifold. These extend the existing mechanism discussion; the main discussion and limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly describes random class/image sampling and use of all corresponding ImageNet validation images, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Appendix B adds annotation, backbone, optimizer, epoch and batch-size details, plus a TorchVision recipe reference for the new tasks.

R1.justification: v4 removes the Tiny ImageNet Visual Recognition Challenge reference and the associated protocol attribution in Section 4.1. The related-work discussion and positioning against synthetic-data, prompting and dataset-distillation research remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the abstract, dataset description and author information, including equal-contribution notation. Three appendix sections are inserted before the retained material, but the main narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v4 adds four quantitative appendix tables, reflows the author block and changes some frequency-series and reference markers in Figure 4. Existing appendix displays are shifted and renumbered; the original plot structures and sample-image grids are preserved.

improvement.justification: The VAE control and synthetic-test analysis address previously untested explanations for transfer failure, while detection and segmentation provide useful corroboration beyond classification. The gain is tempered by evaluation on the same SAM3-labeled image subset, numerical inconsistencies in the new tables, and limited integration of the additions into the main discussion and limitations.
